scope: Exhaustive finite covariance probe for coordinatewise real/imaginary median of three random sketch rows, using gauge-fixed shifts and fourth-root phases.
line_evidence: 6–19 all single-row states; 21–32 all ordered triples and covariance; 35–38 four fixed input examples.
guards: A assumed 2D complex array and M>=2. sumerr has A dtype, so real integer inputs to generic probe can fail during complex accumulation; shown cases explicitly use complex arrays. Mean is reported, not asserted zero.
actual_cost: S=(4K)^(M−1) states and S³ triples. Batch materialization is O(S²KM) memory; covariance accumulation costs O(S³KM²). Exponential diagnostic, never a fast estimator implementation.
assessment: Numerical covariance is finite evidence; the exact witness in source 26 is the stronger counterexample. A basename/header saying independent gives no execution or authorship credit.

scope: Fully enumerated integer Gaussian-arithmetic witness: K=1,M=3,R=3, A=(1,2,3), nonzero off-diagonal median covariance 45/512.
line_evidence: 14–22 sixteen phase states; 23–32 all 4096 ordered triples and exact assertions; 33–35 rational result serialization.
guards: Fixed finite probability space, coordinatewise real/imaginary medians and unnormalized integer input. Exact enumeration and zero means make the asserted covariance a genuine counterexample if arithmetic is evaluated as written.
actual_cost: 16³ triples with constant-size arithmetic, plus integer accumulation. No randomness or floating point affects assertions.
assessment: A finite exact counterexample suffices to refute blanket diagonal median-covariance claims; it does not invalidate separately proved bounds not relying on diagonal covariance. We read every line but did not reproduce the 4096-triple computation.

scope: Finite controls for sketch/DFT factorization, means, variances, risk matrices, heavy tails, median moments, kernel limits, Green fusion and structured/tail cases.
line_evidence: 13–55 operators; 57–92 exhaustive floating identities; 94–120 exact finite moments; 122–163 kernel/Green/structured examples; 166–197 tail controls and output.
guards: Small fixed K,M, odd median sample counts, positive variances and seeded random arrays. Exact Fraction tests cover chosen scalar distributions only. Dense inverses/SVD/ranks and most other equalities use floating tolerances.
actual_cost: Gauge enumeration exponential in M; dense matrices and inverses O(N²) memory/O(N³) work; moment enumeration 5^(M−1) and 3^R. Explicit header correctly says these are reference/test operations.
assessment: Structured success section records residuals rather than asserting every trial succeeds. Bounds and minimax labels in output are supplied theory interpretations, not independently established by a few cases. Does not prove median covariance diagonal; source 26 supplies a counterexample.

scope: Fixed N=256 all-subset parity-cut rigidity reconciliation plus finite general quasiseparable propagation controls.
line_evidence: 3–13 affine data/permutations/field roots; 14–17 compiles and runs sibling C++; 18–30 checks fifteen stored certificates; 31–77 random general-stage controls and result fields.
guards: Exact layout and certificate JSON required, affine permutations checked. Fixed prime roots checked only for order 256. General controls retain zero generators. Assumes the C++ JSON schema and relies on Python assertions.
actual_cost: C++ stage performs 510 dense rank/determinant computations and 3825 flows. Additional Python controls do dense products/ranks at n=4,8,16 for all nonempty stage subsets. This is verification, not a low-cost Fourier evaluator.
assessment: source_code_executed=False in its output distinguishes historical submitted versus reviewer code; the script plainly compiles and executes cut_certificate_own.cpp. It cannot be interpreted as no program execution ever. We executed neither. Fixed-instance cuts do not establish a universal rigidity bound for arbitrary layouts.

scope: C++ finite-field determinant and vertex-capacity flow checker for the prescribed four-stage layout and fifteen replacement subsets.
line_evidence: 9–11 modular Gaussian and Dinic helpers; 12–14 parity sets and two fields; 15–21 graph construction, flow budget checks and JSON.
guards: Assumes valid input n=256 and three permutations; it does not validate n, power-of-two parity balance, index ranges or primality. Constants w=8340,282 are order-256 roots, so changing n without rebuilding assumptions is unsafe. ll products are safe for the two chosen small primes, not arbitrary large moduli.
actual_cost: O(n) parity masks times two O(n³) dense eliminations on n/2 blocks, plus 15(n−1) Dinic flows on O(n) vertices/edges. Retains all parity/flow arrays and rebuilds/copies graphs per mask.
assessment: Exact fixed-instance checker, not generic all-n theorem. Its rank routine assumes square selected minors, and equality of two modular ranks alone is not a characteristic-zero rank proof unless a nonzero witness and upper bound are supplied.

scope: Isolated replay harness for the all-subsets review, copying two programs and two input JSON files into a temporary directory then comparing result bytes.
line_evidence: 3–8 copy, execute and byte-equality; 9 portability output.
guards: Requires a python command on PATH and g++ indirectly through child; check=True catches exit errors. No timeout or assert-enable guarantee. Equality tests one stored expected result file only.
actual_cost: Entire C++/Python checker workload is repeated; file-copy and byte-compare overhead linear in input/output size.
assessment: Historical source_code_executed=False must not erase the obvious execution of reviewer programs in lines 5–7. Portability result is a stored claim, not a replay performed here and not an execution attestation for every inherited dependency.

scope: Exact finite-field controls of Fourier-bank interface uncertainty, CT boundary degrees, Weyl signs, one-sided-sparsity counterexamples and state lifts.
line_evidence: 57–70 exhaustive small uncertainty; 72–95 CT/interface counts; 97–107 Weyl conjugation; 109–135 one-sided and Fourier-containing lifts; 137–170 fourteen-wire residual.
guards: Primitive roots in fixed prime fields, invertible Fourier/bank/exterior matrices. Matrix helpers assume matching nonempty dimensions; inversion fails on singular matrices. n/m/q and root search are not general validated APIs.
actual_cost: Dense O(N³) products/inverses and O(N²) storage; uncertainty enumeration p^m; Weyl cases enumerate m² pairs. Fourteen-wire construction uses 56x56 dense state matrices.
assessment: The one-sided control is expressly not a Weyl pair, and the lifted encoding explicitly contains Fourier data. Neither is a cheap Fourier realization. Finite boundary statistics do not replace a proof across all bank arrangements or a historical novelty comparison.

scope: Batched Fourier-bank/exterior equivalence using interval support covers, fixed-radix conversion, square reverse reduction and calibrated Weyl uniqueness.
line_evidence: 73–90 data and radix maps; 92–115 interval/equivalence cases; 117–134 N²-variable ranks; 136–149 wrong-order and finite configurations.
guards: Radix conversion needs M divisible by Q; reverse two-L reduction only checked when M=Q. j=0 handled separately; cover argument for nonzero active interval uses ceil(Q/j) calls. Noncommuting inverse order is explicitly tested.
actual_cost: Dense verifier O(N³) for identities; uniqueness constructs O(N^4) coefficient storage and Gaussian elimination of N² unknowns, up to O(N^6). Abstract oracle-call counts additionally need O(N) routing and fixed small radix, not free bank transforms for growing radix.
assessment: Tests correctly reject wrong stripping order and retain calibration. Oracle reductions are equivalences with the hard transform cost paid; no new fast exterior or whole Fourier algorithm is established.

scope: Odd-prime Bruhat cell kernels, projective Gauss cocycle and paid word fusion for n=3,5,7,11,13.
line_evidence: 17–28 prime/root/inverse/Gauss tables; 30–43 kernel and cocycle; 44–67 group and exhaustive n=5 pair checks; 68–78 finite words and cost correction.
guards: Parameter modulus n is prime and odd, coefficient p prime with n dividing p−1, and Gauss scalar nonzero. Root selection via w!=1 is sufficient here only because n is prime. b=0 and zero composite b branches explicitly separated.
actual_cost: Source enumerates n^4 candidate group tuples and caches O(n³) matrices of size n², O(n^5) storage; dense products are cubic. Claimed practical fused-word cost is O(t+N) preparation/easy work plus a Fourier call, not this exhaustive checker cost.
assessment: Known group-structure computations and finite controls do not establish a new Fourier engine. Output is relative to current cwd, so identical basename result needs path/hash provenance.

scope: Changed/relocated bank interfaces, low-rank coordinate-swap gauge, affine coset monomial clocks and a finite admissible N=16 exterior construction.
line_evidence: 84–112 relocated actions and gauge support; 114–127 coset controls; 129–153 explicit four-layer exterior identity.
guards: Full active banks and fixed root/field choices; transpose permutation K is involutive. N=16 construction uses zero Green edge masks but nonsingular monomial endpoints; odd cycle steps make Hamiltonian orders. Zero masks are legal only in the stated allowed model.
actual_cost: Dense finite verifier O(N³); relocated Q has row degree M and involves a bank-sized Fourier operator. N=16 endpoint decompositions and basis terms do not supply a uniform all-size construction.
assessment: All four interface actions being monomial does not imply both exteriors are inexpensive; the script itself shows Q row degree M. Do not extend finite N=16 admissibility or zero-mask scope to a strict nonzero-edge model.

scope: Odd-length quadratic-chirp cubic feedback identities, exact degree controls, resonance and full-rank correction at fixed finite-field sizes.
line_evidence: 84–90 field selection; 93–108 chirp powers/Gauss/resonance; 109–127 equivalent B formulas, cubic annihilator and basis Horner evaluator.
guards: Odd n, primitive root, invertible Fourier, Gauss product and 1+c!=0. Resonant n=3,p=7 branch explicitly returns singularity instead of inverting. Minimal degree three qualified by n>=5.
actual_cost: Dense Fourier construction and inversion O(N²)/O(N³); three-B oracle evaluator does not make B cheap. Source explicitly sets B_is_Fourier_oracle_expression=True.
assessment: A low-degree feedback annihilator can coexist with full-rank expensive correction. Dropping that correction destroys feedback. This is a valid scoped algebraic reduction, not a uniform O(N) realization or novelty certificate.

scope: Inverse-support, complementary cut rank, cyclic displacement, sparse-inverse products and low-rank defect telescope controls for the chirp feedback target.
line_evidence: 97–131 guarded target/cuts/rigidity samples; 138–157 inverse factor order; 160–175 telescope; 181–184 diagonal-cancellation and noncontiguous-cut negatives.
guards: 1+c!=0 target guard and each weighted-cycle denominator made nonresonant. Zero weights and singular endpoint diagonals are retained for cut upper bounds. Product sparse-inverse degree only claims invertible monomial-ended factors.
actual_cost: Dense O(N³) inversions/products/ranks over sampled cuts; random row-degree perturbations are finite controls. Product support upper bound grows 2^layers, while rank defects add under telescoping.
assessment: The inverse complementary-block rank identity is the classical mechanism also used by the supplied 0407 cut-rank proof. Noncontiguous cuts can fail full rank, and finite-field diagonal entries can cancel; both limitations are explicitly tested. No blanket all-cut or entrywise-nonzero claim survives.

scope: Explicit N=13 chirp-target two-Green 4x4 minor obstruction for two prescribed noncommuting cycle supports, plus genuine-branch positive controls.
line_evidence: 90–96 four bilinear coefficient columns; 98–120 exact target, orientation, determinant 60131 mod 65521 and half-cut tests; 122–159 zero-edge/singular/monomial controls; 164 decomposability negative.
guards: Prime 65521, primitive thirteenth root, 1+c=41758 nonzero. Offsupport columns and inverse permutation orientation verified. Positive controls distinguish invertible endpoints from singular/zero branches; the nonzero denominator tensor is checked only in invertible branch.
actual_cost: Dense target inversion O(N³); O(N²) row pairs each assembling/ranking an O(N)x4 gate. Entire computation is a finite fixed-support exclusion, not a general lower-bound engine.
assessment: Nonzero modular minor supports nonvanishing after legitimate specialization/denominator clearing, not a theorem over every characteristic. Passing cyclic half-cut budgets shows only that those cuts miss this example; it does not establish novelty or rule out all other classical obstructions. Rank<=3 remains only necessary because decomposability is separate.

scope: Exact chord determinant identity, finite sharp examples, an explicit finite-field failure of a complex-only geometric lower bound, zero-column branch and support-budget arithmetic.
line_evidence: 8–25 determinant/sandwich geometry; 29–33 sharp examples and factor identity; 34–41 field counterexample and zero column; 42–47 reachability budget.
guards: Disjoint chord pairs, nonzero 2-vectors, nonzero division parameters and nonsingular Green denominators in displayed examples. Complex circle geometry is not transported to arbitrary fields.
actual_cost: Dense Fourier sandwiches O(N³), pair enumeration O(N²), root/prime search; support-budget section computes closed forms only and constructs no general evaluator.
assessment: The explicit N=9,F19 union support 6<7 is important scope evidence. The code validates the determinant identity and finite examples but does not itself prove the all-N complex geometric theorem or asymptotic novelty.

scope: Noncommuting Cayley feedback: direct ansatz fails closure; forced conjugation gives quadratic closure and constant-product equivalence, with cut-rank Fourier rejection for larger tested n.
line_evidence: 76–100 direct/forced closure and transfer; 101–110 cut bound; 113–131 general involutions and scalar degree qualification.
guards: Even cycle with shared alternating parity, Cayley denominators at 2 and 3 nonzero, lambda=2 with 1−lambda² invertible. General non-diagonal involution does not imply diagonal Delta; scalar involution reduces minimal degree to one.
actual_cost: Dense verifier O(N³); abstract transfer is a constant product of prescribed structured factors, each still requiring paid application/preparation. Cut-rank budget five applies to the particular shared split and factor geometry.
assessment: Quadratic closure alone does not identify Fourier. The source explicitly rejects direct noncommuting closure and shows forced conjugation may still have an inadequate Fourier cut rank. Classical rank accounting, not proof of a new general method.

scope: Dyadic/coset Fourier ranks, multiscale cut aggregation, Green sum/product budgets and aggregate sparse-fiber recognition with dense fallback.
line_evidence: 31–80 BM/Prony/reconstruction; 83–100 aggregate executor; 112–151 Gram/rank/trie controls; 152–169 Green cuts; 170–204 recognition/full-rank fixtures.
guards: Fixed P=65537 and tested dyadic lengths dividing P−1; aggregate itself does not validate divisibility, positive Q, or root order. Prony always reconstructs raw sequence before accepting and dense fallback requires sufficient remaining budget. Mixed floating Gram and exact modular tests must stay distinct.
actual_cost: Recognition charges selected BM/root/reconstruction terms plus M² heavy fallbacks, but omits some amplitude and inversion work. Output line 99 uses modular pow for each event/bin, adding log N word cost unless phases are precomputed; no phase table/recurrence is used there. Reference DFT is O(N² log N) in modular-power work. Trie control compares to brute force rather than only running the linear aggregator.
assessment: Accepted family can have full fiber-matrix rank and concentrated modes, but is still support-budget restricted. work<=40(N+M budget+budget²) checks only its partial counter, not end-to-end deterministic bit/runtime complexity. Small Green subset loop enumerates one half of masks, not every oriented subset.

scope: Exact rational Banach contraction certificate for one normalized positive-sign F8 factorization into three separated upper/lower-generator stages with repeated bit reversal.
line_evidence: 8–13 data shape; 30–52 scaled product and analytic Jacobian; 53–69 exact inverse/error bounds and sqrt2 enclosure; 70–80 Hessian/self-map/contraction.
guards: 120 center parameters, 64 distinct selected complex variables and 64x64 rational approximate inverse; fixed N=8/stages/permutation. Uses exact Gaussian-integer arithmetic and Fractions for every assertion. Missing pair-length/complete inverse-integer type guards mean malformed JSON is not a fully hardened input format.
actual_cost: Fixed-size dense products and 64-variable rational Jacobian/inverse-residual multiplication; bit costs depend on 60/44-bit input scaling and large derived integers. This is a verification certificate, not a source of exact closed-form parameters or a uniform growing-N algorithm.
assessment: Static proof structure is sound: each output has <=8² monomials of degree <=6, so 30*8²*M^4 bounds the Hessian on radius<=1; eta<1 makes B invertible and contraction fixed point gives equality. Distinct from the adjacent-anchor inverse-sum impossibility proof now subsumed by cut rank. No current recomputation of matrix/Jacobian values.

scope: Independent-method exact rational verification of the same finite F8 local existence data using multilinear unit finite differences rather than analytic Jacobian assembly.
line_evidence: 9–14 candidate identity/shape/types; 27–41 stage product and finite differences; 42–58 rational bounds; 59–62 data hash and saved output.
guards: Parameter tuples and matrix dimensions are checked, though tuple length and scaling-bit types are still trusted. Each variable appears at most once in any path monomial, so a unit real increment recovers the exact complex polynomial derivative. All assertion decisions are rational; float conversion is display-only.
actual_cost: 65 fixed-size stage evaluations plus one dense 64x64 product and exact rational inequalities. Data hashing O(132KB). Not a uniform synthesis/evaluation bound.
assessment: data_sha256 in the stored result binds inert candidate bytes, not the source executable that produced it. Local manifest co-seals source, result and both identical candidate copies. Fresh metadata rechecks can verify that binding and rational inequalities without rerunning this program; the residual/Jacobian numbers remain stored results.

scope: Cyclotomic integer finite audits of Fourier-cycle uncertainty: prime 3x3 full spark, marked-cycle path certificates, monomially scaled sandwiches and coprime-stride composite Vandermonde nodes.
line_evidence: 19–55 cycles/support sets; 58–94 cyclotomic determinant and sandwich; 97–130 prime minors/paths; 133–175 support and composite cases.
guards: All-identical coefficients characterize zero only for the prime lengths used. Cycles must be Hamiltonian, row/column permutations bijective and outer scales nonzero. The composite test uses coprime stride and verifies node distinctness, not arbitrary composite minors.
actual_cost: Exhausts binomial(p,3)^2 minors at p=7,11,13, with length-p coefficient arrays; dense sandwich support checks O(p³) coefficient work plus cycle operations. No fast Fourier engine implemented.
assessment: Correctly states the theorem proof lives in companion text. Finite tests do not replace Chebotarev/full-spark or the general support argument. Supplied code was not executed; no all-field conclusion is drawn.

scope: Fresh-method integer cyclotomic controls for the same support inequalities, including zero weights, singular I−P branches and a concrete p=11 determinant/path decomposition.
line_evidence: 6–29 exact cyclotomic construction/remainders; 36–49 sandwich support; 51–68 prime/composite configurations; 69–80 exact witness and saved output.
guards: Exact monic polynomial divisions and all remainders checked; prime cases allow arbitrary cycles/permutations, composite cases restrict row geometry to affine stride. Outer scales stay nonzero. a=b=1 cases deliberately need not define invertible resolvents, since the sandwich support theorem is broader.
actual_cost: Repeated cyclotomic residue construction, dense four-term coefficient expansions for N² entries and exact support sets. Root polynomials cached, residues rebuilt per case; finite verification cost not a transform bound.
assessment: Zero-weight and resonant sandwich controls do not by themselves authorize inverses at resonance. Preserves characteristic-zero cyclotomic reasoning, distinct from finite-field reduction where minors can vanish.

scope: Even weighted-cycle Cayley family with quadratic loop annihilator, exact scalar cycle-scan evaluator, support/covariance exclusions and resonance/odd-cycle controls.
line_evidence: 71–82 scan; 83–101 parameter preparation; 103–140 closure/transfer/sparse support and basis checks; 142–157 guard negatives.
guards: Even cycle supports alternating parity; char!=2 and lambda=2 needs char!=3. Weighted cycle products must avoid 1 at each relevant scalar. Zero edges and zero operator are intentionally allowed. Lambda=±1 rejected, and odd parity fails as expected.
actual_cost: scan is O(N) arithmetic with one scalar inverse given order/weights; Cayley/three-map output stays O(N) when preparation is paid. This checker instead builds/inverts dense matrices and checks every basis vector, O(N³) work. Parameter search scans field elements.
assessment: Quadratic closure plus a correct Fourier first column does not imply covariance. The sparse denominator support gate excludes Fourier above its bounded threshold, including cancellation branches. A useful structured family, not universal FFT speedup or new-method proof.

scope: Completion of nonzero scales for fixed two-Green inverse directions, using affine graph components, full offsupport checks and explicit recovery of prescribed endpoint permutations/cycles.
line_evidence: 46–84 affine nonzero solver; 85–105 scale system and cycle scan; 108–138 positive recovery; 139–167 incompatible scales/base/resonance/finite-field negatives; 168–176 brute-force small fields.
guards: Each equation has <=2 nonzero coefficients, graph slopes nonzero, free-component forbidden values avoided. Fixed direction base coefficients must be nonzero, cycle products nonresonant, endpoints invertible. F2 free-parameter exhaustion distinct from inconsistent equations; extension to F4 is represented by a hand-checked XOR identity, not a general extension-field solver.
actual_cost: Graph propagation is O(vertices+equations) plus forbidden-value set operations and inversions, but scale_system first forms dense U B V at O(N³); all N² entries checked. Direction search, sparse multiplication implementation and uniform synthesis are not supplied. Negative brute-force checks exponential in nv at tiny fixed fields.
assessment: Passing row eliminations/column nullspaces is insufficient: the N=5 example fails global scale consistency. This closes only the fixed-direction scale problem, not the original unrestricted existence problem. integer_det incidentally uses outer n for sign loops; harmless for its 5x5 call sites, not a generic API.
